parsed.use_case: A reservation management system for shared laboratory hardware must resolve conflicting booking requests for a single device by canceling the fewest reservations possible. This ensures the maximum number of distinct experiments can run without schedule collisions.
system_examples: Google Calendar — resolving overlapping meeting invitations on a single agenda to retain the maximum number of accepted appointments with minimal cancellations.

Astronomical observatory schedulers (e.g., Hubble Space Telescope's SPIKE system) — resolving conflicting observation time slots competing for a single instrument to minimize rejected research proposals.
parsed.explanation: The optimal solution uses a greedy strategy that processes intervals ordered by their end times, reducing an exponential brute-force or O(N^2) dynamic programming approach down to O(N log N). In production systems managing single-resource capacity, this guarantees provably optimal scheduling in near-linear time, preventing costly search overhead under high request volumes.
